verdict.justification: Deliverable B is more faithful to the governance rules specified in the prompt and provides a more comprehensive, tailored document. Specifically, the prompt states that price change requests require approvals from "the Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams." Deliverable B explicitly codifies this as a non-negotiable governance rule ("R2 Price change: Every change to piece price or tooling/one-time cost is approved by Finance Controller, Program Manager and Purchase") and ensures that across all change classes (A, B, and C), all three functions approve at varying seniority levels. In contrast, Deliverable A drops the Program Manager from Class A approvals ("Purchase + Finance controller (delegated). Quality and ER acknowledge; PM informed"), violating the prompt's explicit approval requirement. Additionally, Deliverable B breaks down the Modular Quotation Structure into 8 distinct, practical modules (separating process/conversion, tooling/validation, and locked overheads/margins) and includes concrete proposed thresholds (±2%, ±5%, 10% cumulative anti-fragmentation rule) and Indian context ("DSC/eSign under the IT Act, 2000"). Both deliverables curiously include meta-commentary at the end about "no reference files... found in the working folder," which is unnecessary, though B integrates it slightly better alongside realistic open points and owners.
